## Investment Recommendation

**Rating: Buy**

Dell Technologies exhibits exceptional growth quality, with Q3 FY27 revenue of $54.9 billion surging 103% year-over-year, driven by AI-Optimized Servers revenue reaching $22.0 billion. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=15] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=51] --> This growth is durable, supported by a record $132.3 billion AI backlog and full-year FY27 revenue guidance raised to $202.0 billion, representing a 78% increase. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=30] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=21] -->

Financial resilience is strong, evidenced by $8.6 billion in free cash flow for the fiscal year and operating cash flow of $11.2 billion. <!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=11185000000;2633000000|result=8552000000.0|definition=cash from operations - additions to property and equipment] --> <!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities|period=2025-02-01:2026-01-30|value=11185000000] --> However, financial strength is tempered by negative stockholders' equity of -$2.5 billion, which complicates leverage metrics. <!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:StockholdersEquity|period=2026-01-30|value=-2470000000] -->

The deciding number is the $132.3 billion AI backlog, indicating secured future revenue. The main support is the 103% revenue growth and robust cash generation. The main risk is extreme concentration in the Infrastructure Solutions Group, which now drives the majority of profitability, creating potential volatility if AI demand shifts. The Board’s $25 billion share repurchase authorization signals long-term confidence. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=46] -->

Insight: Dell Technologies' non-GAAP operating expenses fell to 7% of revenue, a level described as the lowest in the company's 42-year history. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=43] -->
